title: Excretion in Humans
seo_title: Secondary 4 Biology: Excretion in Humans Worksheets (O-Level 6093 with Answers)
standard_text: Define excretion and state the excretory products; identify the parts of the urinary system; describe the structure of a nephron and explain ultrafiltration in the glomerulus and selective reabsorption in the tubule; compare the composition of plasma, filtrate and urine; describe the role of ADH in regulating the water potential of the blood; describe the principles of kidney dialysis (summary of the Singapore-Cambridge O-Level Biology 6093 syllabus).
meta_desc: Free Secondary 4 O-Level Biology worksheets on excretion in humans: the kidneys, nephron, ultrafiltration, selective reabsorption, urine, ADH and dialysis. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Filter everything small, then take back what is useful.
key_sub: More ADH → more water reabsorbed → less, concentrated urine.
body_html:
How to think about it

Kidneys remove urea and control water.

  • Excretion removes waste of metabolism: carbon dioxide (lungs), urea, excess water and salts (kidneys).
  • Ultrafiltration: high pressure in the glomerulus forces water, glucose, amino acids, salts and urea into the Bowman's capsule. Proteins and cells stay in the blood.
  • Selective reabsorption: all glucose and amino acids and much water and salt return to the blood.
  • ADH makes the collecting ducts more permeable to water. Dialysis uses a partially permeable membrane and fluid without urea.
Example

Urea 0.03 in filtrate, 2.4 in urine. How many times?

2.4 ÷ 0.03

Answer: 80

Example

Very salty meal. ADH?

blood water potential falls

more ADH

Answer: more ADH, less urine

Common mistakes

  • Calling egestion of faeces excretion.
  • Saying glucose is normally found in urine.
  • Saying proteins are filtered into the Bowman's capsule.
  • Saying ADH makes dilute urine.

faq.q: What is the difference between ultrafiltration and selective reabsorption?
faq.a: Ultrafiltration forces small molecules out of the blood in the glomerulus under high pressure. Selective reabsorption returns useful substances, such as all glucose and amino acids and much water, from the tubule to the blood.
When the blood has too little water, more ADH is released. It makes the collecting ducts more permeable, so more water is reabsorbed and a small volume of concentrated urine is made.
Blood flows past a partially permeable membrane with dialysis fluid on the other side. The fluid has no urea but normal levels of glucose and salts, so urea and excess salts diffuse out of the blood.

items.q: Which structure collects the filtrate from the glomerulus?
items.e: The Bowman's capsule: collects the filtrate from the glomerulus.

items.q: Which structure reabsorbs water under the control of ADH?
items.e: The collecting duct: reabsorbs water under the control of ADH.

items.q: Which organ excretes carbon dioxide?
items.e: Carbon dioxide is made in respiration.

items.q: The kidneys filter 160 dm³ of fluid a day, but only 1.2 dm³ of urine is made. What percentage of the filtrate is reabsorbed?
items.e: (160 − 1.2) ÷ 160 × 100. Almost all the water is reabsorbed.

items.q: What is the role of the proximal convoluted tubule?
c: reabsorbs all glucose and amino acids and much water
brings blood containing urea to the kidney
reabsorbs water under the control of ADH
items.e: The proximal convoluted tubule: reabsorbs all glucose and amino acids and much water.

items.q: What is selective reabsorption?
c: the return of useful substances such as glucose, amino acids, some salts and water from the tubule into the blood
items.e: Glucose is reabsorbed by active transport.

items.q: Is water found in the glomerular filtrate of a healthy person?
items.e: It is small enough to be filtered through the glomerulus.

items.q: What is the role of the bladder?
c: reabsorbs water under the control of ADH
carries urine from the kidney to the bladder
carries filtered blood away from the kidney
items.e: The bladder: stores urine.

items.q: The kidneys filter 180 dm³ of fluid a day, but only 1.2 dm³ of urine is made. What percentage of the filtrate is reabsorbed?
items.e: (180 − 1.2) ÷ 180 × 100. Almost all the water is reabsorbed.

items.q: Is amino acids normally found in the urine of a healthy person?
items.e: All amino acids are reabsorbed.

items.q: What is excretion?
c: the removal of waste products of metabolism and substances in excess from the body
items.e: Egestion of faeces is not excretion.

items.q: Which structure carries urine from the kidney to the bladder?
items.e: The ureter: carries urine from the kidney to the bladder.

items.q: What is ultrafiltration?
c: the filtering of small molecules out of the blood in the glomerulus under high pressure
items.e: The afferent arteriole is wider than the efferent arteriole.

items.q: Is amino acids found in the glomerular filtrate of a healthy person?
items.e: It is small enough to be filtered through the glomerulus.

items.q: The kidneys filter 160 dm³ of fluid a day, but only 1.5 dm³ of urine is made. What percentage of the filtrate is reabsorbed?
items.e: (160 − 1.5) ÷ 160 × 100. Almost all the water is reabsorbed.

items.q: Which structure is a knot of capillaries where ultrafiltration happens?
items.e: The glomerulus: is a knot of capillaries where ultrafiltration happens.

items.q: What is the role of the renal vein?
c: reabsorbs water under the control of ADH
carries filtered blood away from the kidney
is a knot of capillaries where ultrafiltration happens
items.e: The renal vein: carries filtered blood away from the kidney.

items.q: Why is blood pressure high in the glomerulus?
c: The heart is next to the kidney.
The vessel leading in is wider than the vessel leading out.
items.e: This forces small molecules out.

items.q: Is plasma proteins found in the glomerular filtrate of a healthy person?
items.e: Proteins are too large to pass through the glomerulus walls.

items.q: What is the role of the glomerulus?
c: carries urine from the kidney to the bladder
carries urine out of the body
reabsorbs all glucose and amino acids and much water
is a knot of capillaries where ultrafiltration happens
